source.title: Scaling MLPs: A Tale of Inductive Bias
source.authors: Gregor Bachmann; Sotiris Anagnostidis; Thomas Hofmann

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior and compute allocation in vision MLPs, extending scaling-law questions to image pretraining and downstream classification rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own scaling results for downstream vision error, not held-out language-model cross-entropy loss. It does not explicitly test whether fits on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger. It also reports other vision and transfer results that do not bear on the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: New setting. Vision MLPs pretrained on ImageNet21k subsets are scaled in parameters, examples and epochs. The study fits power laws E(C)=a(b+C)^-α+E∞ to linear-probe downstream error and estimates compute-optimal P*(C) and N*(C) following Hoffmann et al. These results bear on V5 (image models), V6 (downstream error versus scale) and V7 (exponents and split vary with setup). No language-model loss is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that MLPs mirror modern models' power-law scaling of downstream error with parameters and examples, and that a lack of inductive bias can be compensated by scale. They also find that compute-optimal MLPs invest far more compute in dataset size (N∝C^0.65 vs P∝C^0.35), which they attribute to weak inductive bias.
record.recipe_differences: Vision MLP pretraining on ImageNet21k and downstream linear evaluation, rather than language-model pretraining loss. The study varies parameters, image examples, and training duration.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture choice changes the reported scaling slope and intercept. The study also reports different scaling behavior when compute is bottlenecked by parameters versus dataset size.
record.problems: The scaling evidence concerns downstream vision classification error, not language-model held-out cross-entropy. The compute-law coefficients are not mapped to individual datasets in the text, and the scaling-law results have no reported uncertainty estimates. The paper does not demonstrate extrapolation from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-law results bearing on the tested versions were omitted. Other transfer-learning accuracies, architecture ablations, and compute-efficiency comparisons are outside the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: All of it: language-model held-out pretraining loss. No upstream (pretraining) loss or error is reported, even for the vision MLPs.
All of it: no fit on small runs is used to predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
All of it: the language-model parameter/token compute-optimal split. The vision analogue is recorded under V5/V7.

All of it. Depth/width at fixed parameter count is not tested for scaling. The Fig. 8 ablations (vision MLP, accuracy at roughly fixed compute) are not readable in the text and are not language models.
Upstream pretraining loss in vision, video, repeated data, and fine-tuning-as-regime scaling. Only linear-probe downstream error of MLPs on 64x64 images is fitted.
Language-model downstream tasks, and downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.

record.verdict_notes: All scaling evidence is downstream linear-probe error of vision MLPs on 64x64 images, fitted with SciPy curve_fit. There are no confidence intervals, and the α-to-dataset mapping is unstated. The allocation estimate fixes T=50 epochs. The record's V3 labels are dropped because the system is not a language model; the allocation finding is carried under V5 and V7. The batch-size, augmentation and transfer results do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy and its power-law dependence on parameters, tokens, or compute.
Explicit out-of-range prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Language-model loss and token allocation; the study tests the analogous allocation of parameters and image examples for downstream vision error.
Whether depth, width, and other architecture details change loss only slightly at a fixed parameter count.
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer as scaling-law regimes; the study tests image-model pretraining and vision downstream evaluation.
Language-model downstream tasks and scaling with language-model pretraining loss; the study tests downstream vision error against compute and model/data scale.

Effects of parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, data choices, and fitting-method alternatives; the study reports differences between MLP architectures and a different compute-optimal allocation from the cited transformer result.

relationships.condition: Vision MLPs (S-MLP and B-MLP, 9M–124M params) pretrained on ImageNet21k subsets, linear-probe error
relationships.reason: Compute-optimal error follows power laws with α 0.12–0.35. The P and N bottlenecks give αP≈1 and αN≈0.35, and P*, N* follow power laws in C (r1–r7).
relationships.display_finding: Compute-optimal error had exponents of 0.12–0.35, parameter- and data-limited exponents were approximately 1 and 0.35, and optimal allocations scaled as powers of compute.

relationships.condition: Linear transfer to CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and ImageNet1k from ImageNet21k-pretrained MLPs
relationships.reason: Downstream test error falls as a fitted power law in compute, parameters and examples for both MLP types (r1, r2, r3, r6, r7). No uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Downstream error decreased according to fitted power laws in compute, parameters, and examples for both MLP types, without reported uncertainty.

relationships.condition: Vision MLPs versus the transformer compute-optimal split, and S-MLP versus B-MLP
relationships.reason: The optimal split is P∝C^0.35 and N∝C^0.65 rather than ≈0.5/0.5 (r4, r5). The fitted slope and intercept differ by architecture, 0.22/0.18 versus 0.25/0.16 (r6, r7).
relationships.display_finding: The optimal split follows P∝C^0.35 and N∝C^0.65 rather than approximately 0.5/0.5 scaling, while architecture changes fitted slope/intercept pairs from 0.22/0.18 to 0.25/0.16.
